sentences.english: Text3 Over the past decade, many compames had perfected the art of creating automatic behaviors - habits - among consumers.
These habits have helped companies earn billions of dollars when customers eat snacks or wipe counters almost without thinking, often in response to a carefully designed set of daily cues.
sentences.translation: 消费者吃零食、擦台面时几乎不假思索，常常是在回应一套精心设计的日常提示；这些习惯帮助企业赚取了数十亿美元。

sentences.english: "There are fundamental public health problems, like dirty hands instead of a soap habit, that remain killers only because we can't figure out how to change people's habits," said Dr. Curtis, the director of the Hygiene Center at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine.
sentences.translation: 伦敦卫生与热带医学院卫生中心主任柯蒂斯博士说，一些基本公共卫生问题，例如不用肥皂洗手、让手保持脏污，仍在致人死亡，原因就在于人们还没找到改变行为习惯的方法。

sentences.english: "We wanted to learn from private industry how to create new behaviors that happen automatically."
sentences.translation: 她说，我们希望向私营企业学习，了解如何让人们自然而然地形成新的行为。

sentences.english: The companies that Dr. Curtis turned to - Procter & Gamble, Colgate- Palmolive and Unilever - had invested hundreds of millions of dollars finding the subtle cues in consumers' lives that corporations could use to introduce new routines.
sentences.translation: 柯蒂斯博士求助的宝洁、高露洁棕榄和联合利华，已经投入数亿美元，寻找消费者生活中那些企业可以利用来引入新习惯的细微提示。

sentences.english: If you look hard enough, you'll find that many of the products we use every day - chewing gums, skin moisturizers, disinfecting wipes, air fresheners, water purifiers, health snacks, teeth whiteners, fabric softeners, vitamins - are results of manufactured habits.
sentences.translation: 仔细观察就会发现，许多日用品——口香糖、润肤品、消毒湿巾、空气清新剂、净水器、健康零食、牙齿美白剂、衣物柔顺剂和维生素——都是人为塑造习惯的结果。

sentences.english: A century ago, few people regularly brushed their teeth multiple times a day.
sentences.translation: 一个世纪前，很少有人习惯每天刷牙多次。

sentences.english: Today, because of shrewd advertising and public health campaigns, many Americans habitually give their pearly whites a cavity-preventing scrub twice a day, often with Colgate, Crest or one of the other brands.
sentences.translation: 如今，由于精明的广告和公共卫生宣传，许多美国人习惯每天两次清洁洁白的牙齿以防蛀牙，常常使用高露洁、佳洁士或其他品牌。

sentences.english: A few decades ago, many people didn't drink water outside of a meal.
sentences.translation: 几十年前，许多人不在用餐时间以外喝水。

sentences.english: Then beverage companies started bottling the production of far-off springs, and now office workers unthinkingly sip bottled water all day long.
sentences.translation: 后来，饮料公司开始把远方的泉水装瓶销售，如今办公室职员会整天不假思索地喝瓶装水。

sentences.english: Chewing gum, once bought primarily by adolescent boys, is now featured in commercials as a breath freshener and teeth cleanser for use after a meal.
sentences.translation: 口香糖过去主要由青春期男孩购买，如今广告将它宣传成饭后清新口气、清洁牙齿的用品。

sentences.english: Skin moisturizers are advertised as part of morning beauty rituals, slipped in between hair brushing and putting on makeup.
sentences.translation: 润肤品被宣传为早晨美容程序的一部分，安排在梳头与化妆之间使用。

sentences.english: "Our products succeed when they become part of daily or weekly patterns," said Carol Berning, a consumer psychologist who recently retired from Procter & Gamble, the company that sold $76 billion of Tide, Crest and other products last year.
sentences.translation: 刚从宝洁退休的消费心理学家卡萝尔·伯宁说，当产品成为人们每日或每周生活模式的一部分时，它们就成功了；宝洁去年销售了760亿美元的汰渍、佳洁士等产品。

sentences.english: "Creating positive habits is a huge part of improving our consumers' lives, and it's essential to making new products commercially viable."
sentences.translation: 她说，培养积极习惯是改善消费者生活的重要部分，也是让新产品在商业上可行的关键。

sentences.english: Through experiments and observation, social scientists like Dr. Berning have learned that there is power in tying certain behaviors to habitual cues through ruthless advertising.
sentences.translation: 通过实验和观察，伯宁等社会科学家认识到，利用强势广告将某些行为与习惯性提示关联起来，会产生强大作用。

sentences.english: As this new science of habit has emerged, controversies have erupted when the tactics have been used to sell questionable beauty creams or unhealthy foods.
sentences.translation: 随着这门关于习惯的新科学兴起，当这些手法被用于推销效果存疑的美容霜或不健康的食品时，争议也随之爆发。
